data.text/markdown:
Factor regression in riskquant

The library answers one kind of question: how does one market series move with others? It has four public functions in riskquant.solutions.factor_regression.api:
Function What it does
align_levels Keeps the dates common to all series in a window. Records every dropped observation.
fit_ols Builds return or level rows, checks rank, fits OLS, reports diagnostics and digests.
wald_test Tests a joint linear hypothesis R @ coef = r on one fit.
unit_root_test ADF test of a declared linear combination of levels (cointegration with a declared vector).
The library reports statistics. It does not decide. A diagnostic never stops a fit. A real fault (wrong domain, rank loss, exact identity) raises a named error. The data come from the canonical fixture riskquant.ingest_fixtures.factor_regression: five cases, each one a business question that the risk engine asks.

1. The data and the alignment

Each case is a Polars long frame: one row per series and observed date. A missing observation is an absent row. The series trade on different calendars (TARGET, NYSE, FX, SIX), so align_levels keeps only common dates and records each dropped observation with a reason:
  • OUTSIDE_WINDOW: the date is outside [start, end).
  • NOT_COMMON_DATE: another series has no observation on that date.
Returns are built after alignment. All terms of one row cover the same interval, also across a holiday gap.

Question. Is the EUR level of XLIST_EUR tied to the USD level of XLIST_USD converted to EUR, and is the peer PEER_EUR tied in the same way?Window [2023-01-02, 2026-01-16), aligned dates: 753.
Generating parameters (truth)

data.text/markdown:
2. Is a EUR asset tied to a USD asset converted to EUR?

XLIST_EUR and XLIST_USD are two listings of one claim. The test object is the log combination ||[z_t = \ln XLIST\_EUR_t - \ln XLIST\_USD_t - \ln USDEUR_t .||]The LOG scale converts USD to EUR inside the combination: no pre-converted series is necessary. The vector ||((1, -1, -1)||) is declared, not estimated, so the N = 1 MacKinnon table applies. PEER_EUR shares 70 % of the return driver but has no long-run tie.

data.text/markdown:
3. Calibrate Proxy V1 loadings for a short-history factor

SMALLCAP_EQ_EU listed on 2024-06-03 and misses about 6 % of its trading days. The engine needs a Proxy V1 row (D088), without intercept: ||[X_{target} = \beta_{EU}\,Y(EQ\_INDEX\_EU,\ LOG,\ h) + \beta_{US}\,Y(EQ\_INDEX\_US,\ LOG,\ h).||]The US index closes one session after the target. A one-day return of the US index covers a shifted window, so the daily US loading is too low. The shift is one session out of ||(2h||), so the bias falls like ||(1/h||). It does not vanish: the population US loading is still 0.28 at ||(h = 20||). population_loadings in the fixture gives the exact biased loadings at every ||(h||) (closed form, no simulation). Overlapping ||(h||)-day rows have MA(||(h-1||)) errors: use HAC with lag ||(\ge h - 1||), or set stride = step. A longer ||(h||) is not free. The count of independent ||(h||)-day intervals is about ||(R / h||), so the ||(\pm 2||) se band widens with ||(h||). A longer ||(h||) trades bias for a wider band. The plot shows the population curve (what the regression measures on average), the fitted loadings of this sample path with their ||(\pm 2||) se band, and the long-run truth. On this sample path the fitted US loading lies about 0.2 above the population curve for ||(h = 2||) to ||(20||) with overlapping rows. That is the sampling deviation of one path, not a property of the process. With the HAC band the truth stays inside ||(\pm 2||) se from ||(h = 2||). Truth: ||(\beta_{EU} = 0.90||), ||(\beta_{US} = 0.30||).

data.text/html: Joint Wald H0: loadings = truth (0.90, 0.30). chi2 p = 0.1576. With IID on overlapping rows the standard errors are too small and a true H0 is rejected; the diagnostic OVERLAP_NOT_CORRECTED says so.
Proxy V1 authored terms from this fit. Provenance: spec_digest=de298a488661e227..., sample_digest=d77a1d42fc160559..., riskquant.factor_regression/1.

data.text/markdown:
4. Factor loadings for the credit VaR copula

The multi-factor Gaussian copula needs, per obligor, the loadings on the systematic factors and the R² (the copula correlation). Equity log returns are the asset-return proxy. Rows are weekly and non-overlapping (step = stride = 5). A volatility regime (August to October 2024, volatility times 2.5) makes the residual variance move with the regressors, so IID and HC0 standard errors differ. The window starts on 2023-07-03, half a year after the first observation: see the OUTSIDE_WINDOW exclusions in section 1.

data.text/markdown: Read the table as follows. The slopes are close to the generating slopes. The US industrial has no European loading, and the test does not reject that. R² is a noisy estimate of the copula correlation on 126 weekly rows: about 13 of them fall in the stress regime and carry most of the variance.

5. Two drivers that carry one signal

German power on two gas hubs (TTF, THE) whose returns correlate about 0.998, and on TTF quoted per MWh and per therm. The condition number ||(\kappa||) is computed on the column-scaled design. The declared threshold is 30 (Belsley, Kuh and Welsch).

data.text/html: The standard error of each hub slope grows about 17 times. The sum of the slopes stays well measured: Wald H0 sum = 0.85, p = 0.404.

data.text/markdown:
6. Rates that cross zero: spreads and trends

CHF two-year rates fall through zero. A log return is undefined, so rates use DIFFERENCE rows and LEVEL-scale combinations. Two spreads:
  • swap minus government: stationary around a constant;
  • covered minus swap: stationary around a trend of 25 bp per year.
Only the matching deterministic case detects the second one.

7. Canonical catalog self-check

The fixture records the outcome of every canonical analysis. This table runs them all through the facade and compares. The fixture tests assert the same table.
